title: Soup enables custom AI training on laptops, cutting GPU needs to #SoupAI #AITools #machinelearning
description: Soup enables training custom AI models on a laptop by drastically reducing GPU memory requirements from 16 GB to just 3.3 GB. Developed by a solo engineer, this open-source tool allows users to fine-tune large language models using simple YAML configurations and a single command, making AI training accessible without expensive cloud resources. This innovation tackles the high cost and complexity of fine-tuning models, which typically demands renting cloud GPUs and managing intricate code. By loading and training models layer by layer, Soup achieves production-grade speeds on modest hardware, democratizing AI development for independent engineers and smaller teams. As Soup gained viral attention on Hacker News, it highlights a significant shift toward more affordable, user-friendly machine learning tools. This could accelerate experimentation and customization in AI, lowering barriers in a field dominated by resource-intensive methods. #SoupAI #CustomAI #AILocalTraining #OpenSourceAI #LLMFineTuning #AIInnovation #MachineLearningTools #HackerNewsViral #AIForEveryone #KazakhstanEngineer #AIResourceEfficiency #ModelTraining #LowMemoryAI #CuttingEdgeAI #TechDemocratization

top_comments.text:
My god what are you talking about

nothing gets "trained layer by layer" here. base stays frozen the entire run. layer streaming just pulls the frozen weights into vram one decoder layer at a time for the forward, then dumps them. the lora adapters are the only thing getting optimizer steps and they all update together in one normal backward. what you described is greedy layer-wise training, totally different thing.
also the 4gb / 119 tok/s isn't from "a tester", that's the maintainer's own 3050 benchmark, it's right there in the readme.
